ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows, in order from left to right, the process of a bacteriophage infecting a bacterium, labeled A, B, C, D, E. A shows the bacteriophage attached outside the host bacterial cell, B shows bacteriophage DNA entering the host cell, the C panel is labeled “phage DNA replicates,” and replicated bacteriophage DNA and many viral components can be seen inside the host bacterial cell, but complete new bacteriophages have not yet formed; D shows “new bacteriophages form,” and E shows new bacteriophage particles being released from the host bacterial cell. Reasoning: In the lytic cycle of bacteriophage infection, the stage in which viral DNA replicates and viral components are synthesized is called biosynthesis. Because C corresponds exactly to bacteriophage DNA replication and viral part production, rather than assembly or release, C marks the Biosynthesis stage.

raw_record.question_text: What stage of a bacteriophage infection is marked C in the figure?

method.method_draft: First inspect the diagram from left to right and locate label C. Note that C is the panel where phage DNA is shown replicating inside the host bacterial cell and many viral parts are present, but complete new bacteriophages have not yet formed. Match this activity to the lytic-cycle terminology: replication and production of viral components inside the host is the biosynthesis stage. Therefore C is Biosynthesis.
